chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Mansur ibn al-Abbas, from Ismail ibn Sahl, who said:
I wrote to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'Excessive debt has bound me.' So he wrote: 'Frequent the seeking of forgiveness, and moisten your tongue with the recitation of "Indeed, We revealed it".'

key_terms.إِنَّا أَنْزَلْنَاهُ: Indeed, We revealed it (referring to Surah Al-Qadr)
key_terms.رَطِّبْ لِسَانَكَ: Moisten your tongue (i.e., make it habitual to recite)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq recommend for relieving debt?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) advises a companion burdened by heavy debt to engage in frequent *istighfar* (seeking forgiveness) and to regularly recite Surah Al-Qadr, linking spiritual purification with material relief. This advice reflects the Shia scholarly understanding that consistent remembrance and repentance can unlock divine mercy and alleviate worldly trials, including financial distress.

en.hubeali: Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Mansour Bin Al Abbas, from Ismail Bin Sahl who said, ‘I wrote to Abu Ja’farasws,
‘Excessive debts have bound me’. So heasws wrote: ‘Frequent from the seeking of Forgiveness, and moisten your tongue with the recitation of [97] We have indeed revealed this (the Chapter)’.
